definitions.explanation: An aesthetic concept valuing beauty found in imperfection, simplicity, and the transient nature of things. One half of the well-known pair {侘|わ}び{寂|さ}び (wabi-sabi).

examples.english: To feel the beauty of wabi.

examples.japanese: ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{侘|わ}び⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{精神|せいしん}→精神：03377_seishin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{根付|ねづ}いている→根付く：13113_nezuku⟧。
examples.english: The spirit of wabi is deeply rooted in the tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: {千利休|せんのりきゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{侘|わ}び⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{美学|びがく}→美学：13914_bigaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{茶|ちゃ}の{湯|ゆ}→茶の湯：14088_chanoyu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中心|ちゅうしん}→中心：01467_chuushin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{据|す}えた→据える：12796_sueru⟧。
examples.english: Sen no Rikyu placed the aesthetics of wabi at the center of the tea ceremony.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{侘|わ}び is a core Japanese aesthetic concept, strongly associated with the ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧ (tea ceremony), especially as developed by {千利休|せんのりきゅう} in the 16th century. It values simplicity, humility, and finding beauty in imperfection.

RELATED WORDS:
- {侘|わ}び{寂|さ}び — the combined aesthetic of wabi (rustic simplicity) and sabi (the beauty of aging and patina). This pair is one of the most widely known Japanese aesthetic concepts internationally.
- {侘|わ}び{茶|ちゃ} — wabi-style tea, a simple and austere approach to the tea ceremony

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally from the verb {侘|わ}びる (to feel lonely/desolate), the concept evolved from a negative sense of loneliness into a positive appreciation of quiet, humble beauty.
